methods.label: Use parallelism to force the second intersection
methods.explanation: If \(c\) did not intersect \(b\), then \(c\parallel b\). Together with \(a\parallel b\), this would imply \(c\parallel a\), contradicting the fact that \(c\) and \(a\) intersect. Therefore, \(c\) also intersects \(b\). Lines \(a\) and \(b\) do not intersect, so there are 2 intersection points in total.
methods.levelReason: The method uses the Grade 7 definition and common-parallel-line corollary, with elementary intersection counting.
